 Order

This criminal petition is preferred under Section 482 of Cr.P.C praying to quash the charge sheet dated 15.06.2016 filed in connection with Crime No.8/2016 of Yamakanmaradi police station and to quash the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 08.01.2021 passed by the Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Sankeshwar in C.C. No.491/2016, convicting and sentencing the petitioners/ accused Nos.1 to 5 for the offence punishable under Section 498(A) R/w. 34 of IPC.

2. Vide impugned judgment and order noted supra, the petitioners have been sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for two and half years and to pay a fine of Rs.2,000/- each for the offence punishable under Section 498(A) R/w. 34 of IPC and in default of payment of fine, to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one month.
Criminal appeal preferred by the accused persons in Crl. A. No.20/2021 against the impugned judgment is pending on the file of V Additional District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. Heard the learned counsel for petitioners, the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 and the learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for State.
4.

An affidavit has been filed by respondent No.2/ complainant, namely the wife of petitioner No.1 stating that during the pendency of the appeal before the Sessions Court, her husband, in laws and herself have decided to resolve the marital dispute existing between them and to lead a happy marital life.
It is also stated that she is currently residing along with her husband and in laws and all of them are living together peacefully without any dispute and quarrels since October-2022.
5. Both the parties are present before the Court.
The respondent No.2/ complainant submits that in fact she has been residing along with her husband since October- 2021 and by inadvertence it is mentioned as October-2022 in the affidavit.
She submits that in view of the peaceful resolution of the disputes, she has no objection if the conviction order passed against the petitioners are set aside.

6. The learned counsel for petitioners has drawn the attention of the Court to the order sheet dated 08.11.2021 in Crl. A. No.20/2021, wherein a submission was made before the learned Sessions Judge that the parties have settled the matter and they are residing together.
Petitioners' counsel submits that the criminal appeal is still pending before the Sessions Court.

7. Hon'ble Apex Court in 'Ramagopal and Another V/s. State of Madhya Pradesh' reported in 2021 SCC Online SC 834 has held at para No.13 as under;
13.

It appears to us that criminal proceedings involving non-heinous offences or where the offences are pre-dominantly of a private nature, can be annulled irrespective of the fact that trial has already Raju S/O Shivaji Gadiwaddar vs The State Of Karnataka on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163880911/
3 been concluded or appeal stands dismissed against conviction.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Handing out punishment is not the sole form of delivering justice.
Societal method of applying laws evenly is always subject to lawful exceptions.

It goes without saying, that the cases where compromise is struck post conviction the High Court ought to exercise such discretion with rectitude, keeping in -view the circumstances surrounding the incident, the fashion in which the compromise has been arrived at, and with due regard to the nature and seriousness of the offence, decides the conduct of the accused, before and after the incidence.
The touchstone for exercising the extra- ordinary power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. would be to secure the ends of justice.
There can be no hard and fast line constructing the power of the High Court to do substantial justice.

A restrictive construction of inherent powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. may lead to rigid or specious justice, which in the given facts and circumstances of a case, may rather lead to grave injustice.

On the other hand, in cases where heinous offences have been proved against perpetrators, no such benefit ought to be extended, as cautiously observed by this Court in Narinder Singh v. State of Punajab and Laxmi Narayan (Supra).

entities.text: Narinder Singh v. State of Punajab and Laxmi Narayan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In the case on hand, the petitioners were convicted by the trial Court for an offence punishable under Section 498(A) Rw.34 of IPC.
The appeal preferred by the petitioners are pending before the Sessions Court.
The parties have filed an affidavit stating that they have resolved the entire dispute and it is also stated that respondent No.2 is staying along with her husband and in-laws since October- 2021.
The offence alleged is predominantly private in nature.
The Hon'ble Apex Court has permitted such compromise to be recorded post conviction by the High Court exercising it's jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.

Hence, in the light of the decision of the Apex Court noted supra, it is just and proper to exercise the inherent power vested in this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C and to quash the proceedings, to meet the interest of justice.

9. Accordingly the following;
 ORDER  i) Petition is allowed.

ii) The conviction and sentence passed against the petitioners by the Court of Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Sankeshwar dated 01/08/2021 in C.C. No.419/2016 for the offence under Section 498-A R/w. 34 of IPC is hereby set aside.

entities.text: Court of Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Sankeshwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: iii) The entire proceedings against the petitioners are quashed.
